t: This is the site of the Museum of Practical Geology, at 28 Jermyn Street. The building is now demolished, so what you see is only where it stood. It was commissioned by Henry De la Beche, the first director of the Geological Survey of Great Britain, who helped pioneer early geological survey methods. He was also a slave plantation owner in Jamaica. The architect was James Pennethorne, who is particularly associated with buildings and parks in central London.
